name: Nullframe Ghost Balaclava — Port-Open Cut
description: A close-fit balaclava in matte signal-absorbing charcoal stretch-knit, leaving only the eyes exposed. Precision-cut port access panels at the occipital and temporal positions are finished with flat-lock seams and sit flush when unoccupied — no sagging or bunching. A secondary half-face filter layer is integral, not removable. The fabric has a faint crosshatch texture visible only at close range.
functionality: Neural-port access panels allow BCI plug-in without removal. Low-emissivity lining reduces thermal signature slightly. Integrated filter handles particulate and light chemical exposure. Fits snugly under helmets or hoods without bunching.
what_it_says: You move through spaces where being seen is a liability, and your chrome is not decorative.
worn_by: Tier 3 night workers with BCI rigs
story_hooks: Nullframe's port-open panels are cut to a spec that matches Axiom Defense neural jack placements exactly — either a coincidence or someone inside Axiom fed the pattern to a street label.
A Tier 4 compliance officer was found wearing one during an internal audit — the footage shows her plugging into a terminal she had no clearance for.
Three different operatives from competing firms showed up to the same location wearing identical Nullframe balaclavas on the same night. None of them know how that happened.
related_entities: Meridian Munitions Compact Machine Pistol CMP-4 'Jackrabbit'
